summary:
The name of this bill is Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 2026 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to amend and integrate existing laws to prohibit employing children in factories, mines, or similar other hazardous work or business, and when employing children in other work, to make such work safe, systematic, and dignified without adversely affecting their health, safety, morality, educational activities, and development (Preamble, Page 1). This Act shall come into force on the thirty-first day from the date of certification (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The Government of Nepal, provincial governments, and local levels shall maintain records of information and statistics of actions taken under this Act (Section 34, Subsection 1, Page 12). The local level shall inspect workplace of child employment at least once every three months (Section 14, Subsection 1, Page 6). The local level shall forward received complaints to the office within seven days and send its recorded information and statistics to the provincial ministry looking after child labor and to the federal Ministry (Section 22, Subsection 3, Page 9; Section 34, Subsection 2, Page 12). The local level shall arrange alternative care and rehabilitate children removed from work until they reach eighteen years of age (Section 16, Subsection 1, Page 7). The Government of Nepal, provincial government, or local level may operate rehabilitation centers for the rehabilitation of children (Section 16, Subsection 2, Page 7). The provincial ministry looking after child labor shall receive information from the local level, and the federal Ministry shall maintain an integrated record of the received information and statistics (Section 34, Subsection 2, Subsection 3, Page 12-13). The Government of Nepal may make rules for the implementation of this Act, and the Ministry may make necessary guidelines, procedures, or standards (Section 36, Page 13; Section 37, Page 13).

Under this Act, employers include individuals or establishments employing children as workers, managers in the case of establishments, and worker suppliers in the case of supplied workers (Section 2, Clause jh, Page 2). No one shall employ a child who has not completed fifteen years of age in work other than work related to child development (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 2). Children who have completed thirteen years of age may be employed in light work pursuant to Schedule-1 with the consent of the child and their father, mother, or guardian (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 2). No one shall employ children in hazardous work or business pursuant to Schedule-2 or against their will (Section 3, Subsection 3, Page 2; Section 4, Page 3). An employer operating a hazardous work or business shall give written notice to the office within thirty days of operation or within thirty days of commencement of the Act (Section 5, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Page 3). An employer employing a child shall submit detailed information along with a photo of the child to the office through the local level within thirty days of employment or within thirty days of commencement of the Act (Section 6, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Page 3-4). An employer shall get the child's health examined before employment and annually thereafter, submit the report, bear all expenses, and for existing child workers, conduct the health examination within thirty days of commencement of the Act (Section 7, Subsection 1, Subsection 3, Subsection 4, Page 4). The employer shall provide necessary training before employing a child (Section 8, Page 4). The employer shall not employ a child from six pm to six am (Section 9, Subsection 1, Page 4). The employer shall not employ a child for more than six hours a day and thirty-six hours a week, and for children between thirteen and fifteen years of age in light work, not more than two hours a day and twelve hours a week (Section 9, Subsection 3, Page 4). A rest period of half an hour after every three hours of continuous work and one day of paid weekly holiday must be provided (Section 9, Subsection 4, Page 4). A child shall not be employed under more than one employer on the same day (Section 9, Subsection 6, Page 5). Equal remuneration shall be paid for work of equal value without discrimination, remuneration and allowances shall not be less than prescribed under labor laws, and enrollment in the Social Security Fund is mandatory (Section 10, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Subsection 3, Page 5). Prescribed safety and health standards must be adopted (Section 11, Subsection 1, Page 5). A register containing details must be maintained and produced or submitted upon request (Section 12, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Subsection 3, Page 5-6). Legal provisions must be posted on the notice board, and a self-declaration must be submitted and posted within thirty days of establishment or commencement of the Act (Section 13, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Page 6).

Licensing provisions are not stated in the bill (not stated in the bill). Regarding health testing, an employer shall get the child's health examined by a health institution before employment and annually thereafter and submit the report to the office through the local level (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 4). If the child's health status appears adverse during the health examination, the child shall not be employed (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 4). Regarding safety and health standards, the employer shall adopt standards prescribed under existing law and additional prescribed standards for the safety and health of child workers (Section 11, Subsection 1, Subsection 2, Page 5).
